newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called down on Iraq, Mexican port news.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called down on Iraq, Mexican port news.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called lower Tuesday on news Mexican crude ports had reopened and statements by an Iraqi official that oil from the oil-for-food deal could be shipped next week, traders said.
"Crude should come back now that you have the ports reopening soon, and Iraq saying oil could be flowing in a matter of days," said a trader.

Crude was called 20 to 25 cents a barrel lower. Refined products were called 0.50 to 0.75 cent a gallon lower. Dealers attributed part of the lower call to profit-taking after a sharp rally in the oil complex Monday, lead by gasoline.

On Monday, January crude settled $1.05 higher at $24.80 a barrel. January heating oil finished up 1.89 cents at 73.57 cents a gallon while January gasoline ended up 2.66 cents a gallon at 68.12 cents.
Boosting crude prices was the shut down of Mexico's three crude ports being closed due to bad weather. Tuesday morning port captains said the ports had reopened.

Meanwhile, senior under-secretary at Iraq's oil ministry, Taha Hmud Mosa, said Baghdad had signed deals with 50 companies to sell Iraq crude and that oil should start being shipped next week under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
The deal will ease U.N. sanctions against Iraq and allow Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months in exchange for humanitarian aid.

The U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq is expected to convene Tuesday at a regularly scheduled meeting to discuss several issues, among them a four-month old charge by the United States that Iran aided Iraq in smuggling gasoil through Iranian waters, U.N. diplomats said.
The U.N. sources said the U.S. charges are unrelated to Iraq's oil-for-food deal.
Tuesday evening, the American Petroleum Institute is expected to release its weekly oil inventory data.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
